tuyuria:abstract:1.title: The earliest stem edestoid (Eugeneodontiformes, Chondrichthyes) from the Viséan (lower Carboniferous) of Tula Region, Central Russia, and a revision of Edestoidea (abstract)

facts.statement: Fossils of Tuyuria were found in Tula Oblast, Russia.
Tuyuria belongs to the superfamily Edestoidei within the order Eugeneodontiformes.
A new family, Lestrodontidae, was erected to contain Tuyuria.
Tuyuria teeth show a basolingual point of the crown that contacts the labial buttress of the adjacent tooth.
Lateral crown processes are absent in Tuyuria teeth.
The labial canal of Tuyuria teeth opens beneath the labial buttress and connects to the pulp cavity.
Numerous transverse vascular canals permeate the base of Tuyuria tooth crowns.
Tuyuria tooth crowns display pronounced wear facets that are unusual among Eugeneodontiformes.
Researchers suggest the wear facets indicate scissor‑type shearing between opposing tooth whorls or placement within a parasymphyseal tooth series.
The tooth morphology of Tuyuria implies it was adapted to crush hard‑shelled prey such as crustaceans.
